brief: A habit tracker as a garden — daily completion waters plants, streaks bloom, neglect wilts

dominant_strengths: Strong metaphor: plants visibly differ in growth/bloom state, communicating streaks intuitively without legends or instructions.
Pleasant gradient sky-to-soil scene establishes diegetic world; sun, clouds, dirt floor reinforce the garden fiction.
Garden Overview card has clean hierarchy with crisp numeric emphasis and tidy row dividers.
dominant_weaknesses: Massive empty middle band — sky dominates 60% of canvas with only floating clouds, wasting prime real estate.
Plant rendering is crude and inconsistent: emoji-like sprouts, identical silhouettes, blooms read as floating dots rather than flowers.
Wilted/neglected states (Writing, Coding) look nearly identical to healthy sprouts — the core 'neglect wilts' signal is weak.
fix_priorities: Differentiate plant lifecycle stages with distinct silhouettes — seedling, sprout, bud, bloom, wilt — so status is legible at a glance.
Compress vertical space or fill sky with meaningful ambient data (weather = habit health, time of day, growth animation cues).
Refine flower/leaf illustration craft — custom SVGs with shading instead of flat circles stacked on stems.
Add interactive watering affordance and streak tooltips to convert decorative scene into actionable tracker.
rationale.norman_balance: Visceral charm of the garden metaphor outweighs behavioral clarity, while reflective payoff (pride in a flourishing garden) is promised but under-delivered by weak state differentiation.
rationale.intent_fit: Concept maps the brief well, but execution under-expresses the watering/wilting feedback loop that would make the metaphor functionally meaningful.
